  • Manage changes to the corporate card program
  • Review the FX hedging work prepared by the business process team
  • Contribute to treasury projects planned for next year, including a new treasury management system and a banking partner migration

Requirements

  • Around 3 to 4 years in a corporate treasury role
  • Hands on experience preparing cash flow forecasts and variance analysis
  • Strong Excel skills, comfortable managing large spreadsheets and version control
  • Experience with bank administration, letters of credit and bank guarantees
  • An accounting background and a clear understanding of how cash movements hit the P&L and balance sheet
  • Confident dealing with banks and stakeholders at all levels
  • SAP experience is a plus, but experience in another ERP is fine
  • CA or CPA is a plus, not essential

job.title: Senior Category Manager
job.description:
Most category managers inherit a strategy, a way of working, and have little actual influence.

This isn't that.

You’ll be the first category hire in a fast-growing world foods business backed by a global group. It has grown at 25% a year for the past five years. The segments it plays in are growing at 6-8% a year, and there’s still real headroom in its current range at both majors.

The plan now is to take a much bigger slice of its global portfolio into new categories over the next three years. There’s a real first-mover advantage here too, because retailers in these categories deal with a lot of small suppliers, and very few of them walk in with a clear category view.

But what the business needs to capitalise on the opportunity is a category function - and that's where you come in.

A few things make this different from a typical senior category role:

  • You’ll cover several categories across the store, not one or two, so your scope and exposure are broader from the start.
  • The growth model is about big plays into new categories, in segments growing far faster than other, more mature categories.
  • You’ll report to an experienced Marketing Director who doesn’t come from category and wants someone who can lead it. You’ll have your own KPIs, a close working relationship with sales and a clear path to building out a category function as the business grows.

To do this well, you’ll need:

  • Category management experience in FMCG, ideally across more than one category
  • Hands-on experience with Circana, Nielsen or Quantium scan and panel data, and the ability to turn it into insight a non-specialist team can act on
  • A track record leading range review conversations with Woolworths and Coles
  • Comfort building with incomplete data and processes - choosing where to start and taking progress over perfection

If you need everything in place to do your best work, this won’t be for you. If you’ve ever looked at your current role and thought “I could build this properly if someone let me”, it’s well worth a conversation.

The role is based in Sydney's north-west, with one flexible work-from-home day a week.

To express your interest and schedule a confidential chat, email me on andrewc@axr.com.au.

job.title: Finance Transformation Manager
job.description:
The Role

 I’m working with an established Australian telecommunications company that’s growing & expanding their product lines. They need a senior finance person to build the finance side of each one properly.

This is a hands-on role. There’s no team underneath you to delegate to, so you’ll be the one reading the contracts, talking to key business stakeholders, working through the accounting and writing the position papers. Then you’ll build what’s needed in the ledger and the reporting infrastructure supporting it including KPI dashboards.

To start with, you’ll look across the new functional lines, find the real risks and gaps, and agree a plan with Finance leadership and the business owners. From there the work covers technical accounting on revenue, capex, leases, incentives and funding arrangements. You’ll also design the GL and reporting structure, set the finance requirements for Microsoft D365, and build the contract-to-cash flows, reconciliations and controls behind it all. Once each business line is running cleanly, you hand it over to Finance Operations and Financial Control.

You’ll report into senior finance leadership and have a good amount of autonomy. Material policy and commercial calls still go up for approval, but day to day you’re the finance lead on these projects, working closely with Commercial, Legal, Operations, Tax and the executive team.

What they’re looking for

You’re CA or CPA qualified with a long run of senior finance experience, probably 15 years or so. They care a lot more about what you’ve delivered than the number, though. You’ve led complex technical accounting work and you’re comfortable defending your view in front of a CFO. Most importantly, you’ve personally set up the finance for a new business, a major commercial contract or a complex project, taking it from the accounting conclusions through ERP, controls and reporting to the BAU handover.

You’ll need strong GL and ERP knowledge and solid modelling skills, because you won’t have a big support team. Microsoft D365 experience, a good handle on AASB 15 and 16, or a background in telco or infrastructure would all also help.

If this sounds like you, apply here to express your interest. You can reach out to Kunal Gupta at kunalg@axr.com.au for more information.

job.title: Program Manager
job.description:
This isn’t a technical build role. It’s governance — stepping into the final stretch of a major ERP transformation to give the Board confidence that risk is being managed, not just talked about.

This is a 12-month Program Manager contract overseeing the final stages of a major ERP transformation at a mid-size industrial business — largely work-from-home with time in the South-West Sydney office as well, on a highly competitive package for the engagement.

The business is around eight months from go-live, replacing a legacy project-based system with a purpose-built platform widely used across the sector. Experienced in-house technical support are already driving the detail — training, data conversion, UAT. What’s missing is someone above that layer: a program manager who can take governance control, translate the detail into plain, decision-ready updates, and close the gap that’s opened up between the delivery team and the Board. The role works directly with the CEO, CFO and Board.

What the role looks like

  • Take ownership of program governance across the final stages of the implementation — managing risk, derisking what’s left, and giving the Board genuine confidence in progress.
  • Oversee training, data conversion and testing workstreams — tracking status, surfacing gaps early, and making sure nothing’s been missed across the business.
  • Report directly to the CEO, CFO and Board — turning technical detail into clear, decision-ready updates they can act on.
  • Lead the governance of change management — assessing how ready the business really is for the change, and communicating that honestly upward and downward.
  • Coordinate a capable, engaged senior delivery team that’s already bought in — the role exists to close the governance gap between that layer and the Board, not to fix a broken team.

What you’ll need

  • Proven experience running governance or program management on a large-scale ERP or systems transformation
  • A track record of reporting confidently to C-suite and Board level, translating technical complexity into plain language
  • Strong stakeholder management — the ability to push back and hold people to account without burning relationships.
  • A solutions mindset — you bring the Board options and recommendations, not just a list of problems.
  • Exposure to industrial project-based businesses and/or leases is useful, but not essential.
  • Hands-on and flexible early on, with the comfort to settle into a more remote rhythm once you’re across the detail.

What makes this worth your time

  • A high-visibility mandate with a direct line to the CEO, CFO and Board at a pivotal point in a major transformation.
  • Genuine autonomy to set the governance rhythm — you’re closing a gap in an otherwise well-run program, not inheriting a mess.
  • A highly competitive package for a focused, time-boxed engagement.
  • Mostly remote work, with periodic travel to the head office and occasional site visits
  • Immediate start — the role is signed off and ready to go.

This process will move fast — the role’s signed off at Board level and they want someone in seat as soon as possible. Apply now or reach out to Dave Goldbach for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
A large privately owned business needs a CFO who turns the numbers into plain English and becomes the MD's trusted right hand. This is a true commercial and business partnering CFO role and a key member of the ELT.

This established, successful business is in a period of significant change and growth and needs a leader to help steer it through the next chapter. It’s a hands-on, industrial business with a down-to-earth culture. People work hard, back each other and have a good laugh along the way, so fit with the team matters as much as capability.

About the role

This Chief Financial Officer role is Melbourne-based and office-based, with an executive remuneration package. Reporting to the Managing Director and sitting on the Board, you will lead the Finance function, and be the finance partner the MD can rely on to run the numbers, the governance and the conversation with the executive team. The role entails the following:

  • Build FP&A and business partnering into a sharper commercial capability that tells the ELT where the business is heading, not just where it has been
  • Lead the finance function across financial control, governance, treasury and risk, lifting team performance and building a succession bench
  • Build the financial confidence of the ELT by explaining margin, working capital, cash flow and trade-offs in plain language
  • Challenge assumptions constructively and hold the business to plan, budget, forecast and strategic targets
  • Help drive the IT strategy, including vendor and cost management, cyber risk and getting full value from newly implemented systems
  • Support acquisitions, integration and group-level finance activity as the business continues to grow

Ideal profile

  • Proven CFO or equivalent in a large, complex business. This is not a first CFO role: you have run the numbers at scale and learned from it
  • Confident to say "I think you're wrong" and equally comfortable hearing "you're right", with the humility and EQ to do both
  • A hands-on, commercial operator who is across product, margin and cash, and can explain complex finance to anyone from the Board to the shop floor
  • Product led industries: Industrial, Retail, FMCG and distribution backgrounds all translate. Private, family-owned or PE-backed experience is a real plus
  • Leads with energy and care, with a track record of developing people and lifting the performance of established teams
  • CA/CPA qualified, with MBA or AICD advantageous

The business is ambitious, the executive team is easy to work with, and the MD wants a finance partner who is commercial, credible and genuinely invested in people. If you have been waiting for a CFO seat where you can shape strategy as well as run finance, this is it.

If this sounds like the role for you, please apply through the link or contact Dave Goldbach at daveg@axr.com.au. All enquiries are treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Marketing Director ANZ
job.description:
The Company:

We are a globally recognised business and the clear market leader in our category, with a premium brand trusted by professional users and home consumers alike. Over the past few years, our local leadership team has returned the business to growth and brought Australia and New Zealand together as one Oceania region – a change journey that has delivered exceptionally high employee engagement and recognition as a top employer. With ambitious three-to-five-year growth plans, significant investment in product technology innovation and a deep commitment to our specialist dealer and retail partner network, we're now entering our next phase of growth.


The Role:

Reporting directly to the CEO and sitting on the Executive Leadership Team, the Marketing Director will lead the marketing function across Australia and New Zealand – spanning brand, product marketing, customer engagement and market development. With the campaign strategy shifting and the marketing budget scaling significantly, the brief is to grow market share and brand awareness, broaden understanding of the full product range, and make marketing a genuine commercial engine for the business. You'll lead a team of six direct reports and one dotted-line report, based in Melbourne.


Key responsibilities include:

  • Set the Oceania marketing strategy and framework, aligned to global objectives while giving Australia and New Zealand the freedom to win locally
  • Be the voice of the professional and home consumer, using research and insight to shape strategy and identify growth opportunities
  • Own the marketing budget and ROI – removing waste and making clear choices between brand building and short-term activation
  • Lead go-to-market for product launches, campaigns and seasonal initiatives, including retail marketing and point of sale across the dealer network
  • Reset and lead the agency model across the region, building long-term partnerships that deliver measurable outcomes
  • Set a new standard across digital marketing, social, customer engagement platforms and e-commerce, while building the team's capability

What You'll Bring:

  • Significant marketing experience, including a Head of Marketing or Director role, ideally within FMCG or consumer goods manufacturing
  • Strong commercial acumen, with a sound understanding of trade P&L dynamics and the levers that build or erode brand value
  • Experience with both complex major retailers and fragmented or independent retail networks
  • Broad capability across trade, digital and traditional marketing – and the confidence to translate data from multiple sources into clear choices
  • Multi-market leadership experience, with Australia and New Zealand exposure strongly preferred, plus tertiary qualifications in business, marketing or a related field
  • A humble, hands-on leadership style – close to the work, able to move from strategy to execution, and a genuine builder of team capability

Why Join?

This is a highly autonomous executive role with real scope to shape the function, the market and how the region contributes globally. You'll inherit a passionate team and a strong brand, with a significantly scaled budget and the freedom to build the right agency partnerships. You'll report to a CEO with more than two decades in FMCG and consumer goods across sales leadership, category strategy and shopper marketing – a decisive, empowering leader who coaches by asking insightful questions, keeps an open door and is direct and transparent, so you'll always know where you stand. Add a family-owned culture built on humility, honesty and hard work, and genuine investment in development and international career opportunities, and this is a rare chance to lead a market leader into its next chapter.

job.title: National Account Executive | Premium Food | Sydney
job.description:
The Business
This is an exciting opportunity to join the Australian arm of an established international FMCG business with a strong reputation for quality and a growing presence in the local market. The business has experienced significant growth in Australia and continues to invest in its people, customer partnerships and commercial strategy. Operating within a lean, high-performing team, this is an opportunity to make a genuine impact, work closely with key retail customers and contribute to the next phase of the business’s growth.

The Role The National Account Executive sits at the operational heart of the commercial team. You will be the person who makes sure promotional programmes land correctly, forecasts are accurate, and deadlines are met across Woolworths, Coles, Metcash and key independents. When this role is done well, the Senior National Account Managers can focus entirely on growing the business.

Key areas of responsibility include:

  • Promotional Management — End-to-end ownership of promotional programmes across major grocery retailers. Submitting plans, managing retailer portals (including Woolworths Partner Hub and Coles PAFs), tracking confirmations, and ensuring flawless execution within tight deadlines.
  • Commercial Analysis & Forecasting — Day-to-day sales analysis and performance reporting, supporting S&OP and forecasting cycles in close collaboration with the category team. Your accuracy with data will directly shape the team's ability to plan and execute with confidence.
  • Claims & Trade Spend Management — Managing claims reconciliation across major retail customers and liaising with the international back-office team to ensure trade investment is accurately tracked and processed.
  • Sales Support — Supporting range reviews, new line set-up, customer presentation development, and ad hoc administrative tasks across grocery, foodservice and independent channels.

The Candidate
You don't need to have done this exact role before — but you do need to bring the right mindset: detail-oriented, analytically driven, proactive, and hungry to learn.

You might currently be working in a field sales or key account role within FMCG, or in an analytical capacity at a data agency. What matters most is your attitude and your application.

You will bring:

  • Experience in a sales, account management or analytical role within FMCG or a related field
  • Strong attention to detail and genuine pride in the accuracy of your work
  • Analytical capability, and a desire to continue developing in this area
  • The ability to manage multiple competing priorities without dropping the ball
  • Confidence communicating with senior stakeholders — knowing when to ask, when to escalate, and how to do both well
  • A team-first attitude and the energy to thrive in a small, fast-moving environment
  • Familiarity with IRI, Nielsen or Quantium data tools is advantageous but not essential

Why This Role
This is not just an admin role with a fancy title. It is a genuine commercial position within a business that punches well above its weight. In a team this size, your contribution is visible, your development is real, and your impact is immediate.

If you want to learn the commercial mechanics of FMCG from the inside — this is the role to do it in.

Our flagship brand was created in Australia, leads its category here and is now exported internationally. With a lean marketing team and an ambitious growth agenda, we offer real breadth for someone who wants hands-on exposure across the full marketing mix.

  • Manage the influencer program, from briefing, content development and approvals through to posting schedules and performance tracking
  • Develop and deliver digital, social and content-led campaigns behind new product launches, and identify and manage brand collaborations

  • A degree in Marketing or Business, plus 5+ years' marketing experience
  • A strong focus on digital, social and influencer marketing, with confidence across Meta and TikTok
  • An independent, autonomous self-starter with initiative and a positive, can-do attitude – you see what needs doing and get on with it

  • Curiosity and a real hunger to learn and develop across the full marketing mix
  • An energetic, relationship-driven approach that thrives in a small, close-knit team; FMCG, beverage or food service experience is a plus

Why Join?

This is a chance to take real ownership of the digital agenda for a homegrown brand with global reach, new launches to bring to market and international markets to partner on.
